info.title: Labs API
info.description: API for integrating lab diagnostics — availability checks, package catalog, requests (enquiries), order management, report retrieval, and health camps. Every call must include a valid `ls-api-key` header.

ApiKeyAuth.name: ls-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key issued by LabStack. Pass this in every request header. Your store can hold two active keys at once, so you can move to a new key before the old one is revoked. A key may have an expiry date; a request made with an expired or revoked key is refused as unauthorized.

error.example: Authorisation failed - API Key not present in HTTP Header.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized — API key missing, invalid, expired or revoked

TooManyRequests.description: Too many failed authentication attempts from your address. Every request from that address is refused, whatever key it carries, until the number of seconds in the Retry-After header has passed.

BadRequest.description: Bad request — missing or invalid parameters

requestId.description: Id of the created request. Pass this to Link a request to an order once the order exists.

requestStatus.description: Always OPEN for a newly created request.

orderType.description: Optional. Type of service the customer is interested in.

isVip.description: Optional. Marks the request as VIP. Defaults to false.

referenceId.description: Optional. Your own reference id, echoed back on the request.

requestGroupId.description: Optional. Your own grouping key, to tie several requests raised together into one batch.

packageIds.description: Optional. LS package ids the customer is interested in (e.g. LSP11002). Each must be active and part of your store network, and must support orderType when one is given.

testIds.description: Optional. LS test ids the customer is interested in (e.g. LSL110001).

appointment.description: Optional. Preferred appointment date-time, ISO 8601 format. Must be in the future.

labId.description: Optional. Preferred lab, as returned by List labs. Must be in your store network, support the requested orderType, and carry every package and test given.

notes.description: Optional. Free-text notes for the request (e.g. "Patient is old, veins are thin").

amountPaidToStore.description: Optional. Amount in INR the customer has already paid your store for this request, as a number of 0 or more. Omit it, or send 0, when nothing was paid. When it is above 0, the order booked from the request is set up by default for your store to collect payment from the customer.

name.description: Customer name. Sanitised to alphanumerics and spaces; must be non-empty after sanitisation and at most 50 characters.

dateOfBirth.description: Optional. YYYY-MM-DD. Cannot be in the future. Takes precedence over age when both are given.

age.description: Optional. Customer age in whole years, used to derive an approximate date of birth. Read only when dateOfBirth is omitted.

altContact.description: Optional. Alternate contact number. 10 digits, cannot start with 0.

unitFloorBuilding.description: Optional. Part of the customer address.

address.description: Optional. Part of the customer address.

locality.description: Optional. Part of the customer address.

city.description: Optional. Part of the customer address.

state.description: Optional. Part of the customer address.

example.notes: Customer asked for an early morning slot.
example.name: Bob Smith

post.description:
Creates a request - an enquiry raised against the authenticated store, not an order. Use it when a customer has shown interest but the booking is not yet confirmed: the request is followed up, the details and pricing are settled, and once the order has been placed the two are tied together with Link a request to an order. Only name and mobile are required. Any packages and tests given must be part of your store network, and an optional labId pins the request to a single lab, which must support every package and test given as well as the requested orderType.
If the customer has already paid your store for this request, give the amount in amountPaidToStore. The order booked from the request is then set up by default for your store to collect payment from the customer.

get.description: Ties an existing request to an order that has already been placed. This GET has side effects: on success the request is marked as converted and permanently associated with that order. Both ids must belong to your store, otherwise the call reports that nothing was found. A request can be linked only once, and an order can be linked to only one request - attempting either again fails with a 400 that says so.

referenceId.description: The reference id after the update.

uniqueId.description: The patient's uniqueId after the update.

404.description: Order not found for this store

orderId.description: Order id to update. Must be an order placed by your store.

referenceId.description: Optional. Your own reference id for this order; echoed back in responses and webhooks. Up to 100 characters. Pass an empty string to clear it.

uniqueId.description: Optional. The new uniqueId for the order's patient. Up to 100 characters, and must not already be in use by another of your patients.

post.description: Updates the identifiers you gave an existing order. Send orderId plus at least one of referenceId and uniqueId; anything you omit is left unchanged. referenceId replaces your own reference on the order, and an empty string clears it. uniqueId renames the patient this order belongs to — the patient record itself, so the new uniqueId is what every other order and appointment of theirs reports too. It is rejected with 400 if any other patient of yours already uses that uniqueId — including when the order's own patient already has it, so the same call run twice fails the second time — and with 400 when the patient on the order is not one of yours to rename. Both changes are recorded against the order and are visible to LabStack support.

post.summary: Move a test order to a status (UAT only)

202.description: The order has started moving. Its webhooks follow.

orderStatus.description: The order status when you called. Also the first entry of statusPath.

targetOrderStatus.description: The targetOrderStatus you sent. Also the last entry of statusPath.

statusPath.description: Every status the order will pass through, in order: its current status, then each status it will be moved to, ending with targetOrderStatus. Expect one webhook for each entry after the first.

interval.description: Seconds between status changes: the interval you sent, or 5.

400.description: The order cannot be moved as asked, and error says why. Returned when the body is not a JSON object; when orderId, targetOrderStatus or interval is missing or invalid; when targetOrderStatus is not in the row for the order's type (error lists the allowed values); when the order has already reached or passed targetOrderStatus; and when the order is CANCELED, PATIENT_MISSED, PHLEBO_NO_SHOW or SAMPLE_REJECTED.

orderId.description: Id of the order to move, as returned by placeOrder. Must be one of your orders.

targetOrderStatus.description: Status to move the order to. Must be in the row for the order's type in the table above, after the order's current status.

post.description:
Available only in the UAT environment; anywhere else it answers 403. Use it to test how your integration handles each stage of an order without waiting for a lab to act on it.

Moves one of your orders forward to `targetOrderStatus`, one status at a time. The call answers 202 straight away with `order.statusPath`: every status the order will pass through, starting with its current status. The first change is made right after the response and the rest follow `interval` seconds apart, so in the example below the order reaches PHLEBO_STARTED about 10 seconds after the call.

The changes are real. The order keeps each new status, and every change appears in its history as it would if a lab had made it.

#### Statuses by order type

Any status after PENDING in the order type's row is a valid `targetOrderStatus`. The order passes through every status between its current one and the target, in this order:

| orderType | Statuses, in order |
| --- | --- |
| `HOME_SAMPLE` | PENDING → CREATED → ORDER_SCHEDULED → PHLEBO_ASSIGNED → PHLEBO_STARTED → SAMPLE_COLLECTED → SAMPLE_IN_TRANSIT → SAMPLE_DELIVERED → SAMPLE_PROCESSED → REPORT_DELIVERED |
| `CENTER_VISIT` | PENDING → CREATED → ORDER_SCHEDULED → PATIENT_VISITED → SAMPLE_COLLECTED → SAMPLE_IN_TRANSIT → SAMPLE_DELIVERED → SAMPLE_PROCESSED → REPORT_DELIVERED |
| `KIT_BASED` | PENDING → CREATED → KIT_BOOKED → KIT_DISPATCHED → KIT_DELIVERED → SAMPLE_COLLECTED → KIT_PICKUP_BOOKED → KIT_PICKUP_IN_TRANSIT → SAMPLE_DELIVERED → SAMPLE_PROCESSED → REPORT_DELIVERED |
| `CAMP` | PENDING → CREATED → REPORT_DELIVERED |
| `SAMPLE_DROP_OFF` | PENDING → CREATED → ORDER_SCHEDULED → SAMPLE_COLLECTED → SAMPLE_DELIVERED → SAMPLE_PROCESSED → REPORT_DELIVERED |

An order whose status is not in its row continues from the next status in the row. A RESCHEDULED order moves to ORDER_SCHEDULED first (KIT_BOOKED for a kit order), and a PARTIAL_DELIVERED order moves to REPORT_DELIVERED.

#### Webhooks and messages

Each change sends your Diagnostics Webhook URL the same order webhook a real change would, with the payload described under Webhook in [Trigger a test order webhook](#get-api-v1-3-order-testWebhook). If your store has no Diagnostics Webhook URL, the order still moves but nothing is sent.

| Status reached | `events` in the webhook |
| --- | --- |
| Any status | `STATUS_CHANGED` |
| PHLEBO_ASSIGNED, when the order had no phlebotomist | `STATUS_CHANGED`, `PHLEBO_CHANGED` |
| REPORT_DELIVERED, when the order had no report | `STATUS_CHANGED`, `REPORTS_CHANGED` |

The patient messages your store has switched on for these statuses are sent too, and so is the report email if your store receives reports by email. Use patients whose contact details are your own.

#### Sample data

Where a status needs details the order does not have yet, sample values are written in the same change, so its webhook carries them. Details already on the order are kept.

| Status reached | Field | Sample value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHLEBO_ASSIGNED or PHLEBO_STARTED | `phleboName`, `phleboNumber` | `Dummy Phlebo`, `9876543210` |
| PHLEBO_STARTED | `phleboStartTime` | The time of the change |
| REPORT_DELIVERED | `reports` | One sample report, whose link downloads a sample PDF |

#### When the order cannot be moved

- A `targetOrderStatus` that is not in the order type's row, or that the order has already reached or passed, is rejected with 400.
- CANCELED, PATIENT_MISSED, PHLEBO_NO_SHOW and SAMPLE_REJECTED orders cannot be moved, and are rejected with 400.
- An order moves towards one target at a time. A second call for the same order answers 409 until the first has finished.
- If anything else changes the order's status while it is moving (a cancellation, say), the remaining changes are skipped and the order keeps the status it was given.

get.description:
Sends one order webhook for an existing order to your Diagnostics Webhook URL, so you can test the endpoint that receives it. The order itself is not changed. If your store has no Diagnostics Webhook URL, nothing is sent and the call still answers success.

The webhook carries the order as it is now, with `events` set to `[STATUS_CHANGED]`. Pass `orderStatus` to see the payload at another stage of the order. The status being sent shapes the payload as follows:

- PENDING, CREATED, ORDER_SCHEDULED, RESCHEDULED and the kit statuses (KIT_BOOKED, KIT_DISPATCHED, KIT_DELIVERED, KIT_PICKUP_BOOKED, KIT_PICKUP_IN_TRANSIT) send `phleboName` and `phleboNumber` as null.
- Every other status except CANCELED fills in a sample phlebotomist when the order has none. PHLEBO_STARTED also sets `phleboStartTime` to an hour before your call.
- Passing `orderStatus=RESCHEDULED` moves `appointmentTime` to 10:00 IST the next day.
- `reports` is empty for every status except REPORT_DELIVERED and CANCELED. REPORT_DELIVERED adds a sample report when the order has none, and its link downloads a sample PDF.

The payload is described under Webhook below. Webhooks sent for real changes to your orders have the same shape.

post.summary: Order webhook, sent to your Diagnostics Webhook URL whenever one of your orders changes
post.description:
Sent as a POST with a JSON body. Answer with any 2xx status; the response body is ignored.

Every webhook carries your store's webhook authentication header, a header name and value agreed with LabStack: check it to confirm the webhook came from LabStack. Contact us to set or change it. Its value does not change when your API keys are rotated or revoked.

`events` lists everything that changed in the update, so one webhook can carry several events:

| Event | Sent when |
| --- | --- |
| `STATUS_CHANGED` | `orderStatus` changed. |
| `RESCHEDULED` | `appointmentTime` changed. |
| `REPORTS_CHANGED` | A report was added to, replaced in or removed from `reports`. |
| `PHLEBO_CHANGED` | A phlebotomist was assigned or replaced, so `phleboName` or `phleboNumber` changed. |
| `LAB_CHANGED` | The order moved to another lab. `labName`, `labLogo`, `lsLabId` and `lsChainId` describe the new lab. |
| `HARMONIZED_VALUES_CHANGED` | The order's standardized test values changed. Fetch them with getReportRawValues. |
| `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` | The payment the order was waiting for came through, and `isPaymentRequired` is now false. |

Every order reports the CREATED status. When an order moves past CREATED in a single step, you are first sent a STATUS_CHANGED webhook with `orderStatus` CREATED, then the one with its new status.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The webhook authentication header most stores receive, holding the webhook key agreed with LabStack for your store. If your store's authentication header has another name, that header is sent instead; if none is set up, webhooks carry no authentication header.

A KIT_BASED order reports KIT_PICKUP_IN_TRANSIT where other orders report SAMPLE_IN_TRANSIT. SAMPLE_REJECTED means the lab could not test the sample; a new collection follows and moves the order on, or the order is cancelled.

post.description:
Records your customer's feedback on one of your orders. `feedbackType` says which survey the feedback answers, and decides the rating scale and the survey answers the body must carry. Send the survey answers as top-level fields next to `rating`; do not wrap them in an object.

| feedbackType | What it rates | rating | Survey fields | Accepted when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SAMPLE_COLLECTION` | The booking and the home sample collection visit | Whole number from **1 to 5** | `phleboOnTime`, `goodPhleboBehavior`, `easyBookingProcess`: all three required, each `true` or `false` | The order is a `HOME_SAMPLE` order, is not `CANCELED` or `PENDING`, and its appointment time has passed or its sample has been collected |
| `ORDER_COMPLETE` | How likely the customer is to recommend the service | Whole number from **1 to 10** | None | The order is `REPORT_DELIVERED` |

A survey field of the other feedbackType, a missing survey field, or a rating outside its type's range is rejected with 400. `comments` is optional for both types.

An order holds one feedback per feedbackType: submitting the same feedbackType again for the same order replaces the earlier rating, survey answers and comments. A low rating opens an escalation on the order for LabStack support to follow up.

Example `SAMPLE_COLLECTION` body:

```json
{
  "orderId": 47585,
  "feedbackType": "SAMPLE_COLLECTION",
  "rating": 4,
  "phleboOnTime": false,
  "goodPhleboBehavior": true,
  "easyBookingProcess": true,
  "comments": "The phlebotomist arrived 20 minutes late but was very gentle."
}
```

Example `ORDER_COMPLETE` body:

```json
{
  "orderId": 47585,
  "feedbackType": "ORDER_COMPLETE",
  "rating": 9,
  "comments": "Reports arrived on time."
}
```

get.description: Reschedules an order to a new appointment time (validates slot availability with the lab). An order cannot be rescheduled within 30 minutes of its current appointment time, or once that time has passed. This GET has side effects.

Either your store already has an active order for this uniqueId with exactly the same packageIds and testIds and an appointment on the same date (orderId, referenceId and orderStatus identify it), or an identical request is still being processed (error only; retry after it completes).

post.description: Creates an order for the authenticated store. Provide packageIds and/or testIds. pincode is always required; address/city/state are additionally required for HOME_SAMPLE orders. Either dateOfBirth or age must be provided. For a patient already on record (same uniqueId), a recorded gender or date of birth is kept, and is what the lab receives, even if this request sends different ones; only a value not yet recorded is taken from the request. Use POST /api/admin/v1.0/user/updateUserDetails to change them. orderType CAMP is not accepted by this endpoint. uniqueId is optional (auto-generated when omitted). Optionally returns a payment link when payment is required; that link is valid for 16 minutes and the order is auto-cancelled if payment is not completed in that window. Once payment completes the order is retained, getOrderDetails reports isPaymentRequired as false, and an order status webhook is sent carrying the PAYMENT_RECEIVED event. Returns 409 when your store already has an active order for the same uniqueId with exactly the same packageIds and testIds and an appointment on the same date (IST), at any time of that day and regardless of address or orderType. The same items on another date are a new order. An order stops being active once it reaches REPORT_DELIVERED, CANCELED, PHLEBO_NO_SHOW, PATIENT_MISSED or SAMPLE_REJECTED. Reschedule or cancel the existing order (its orderId is in the 409 response) instead of placing it again. referenceId is not used to detect duplicates. If a call times out, look the order up with getOrderDetails by your referenceId before retrying, and retry with the same request body only if it is not found.

packageId.description: LS package id (e.g. LSP10002) of the package the test was reported under, when known.

profileId.description: LS id of the profile the test belongs to, when it is part of one.

testId.description: LS test id (e.g. LSL100018). Always present, and distinct where the same test name is used for different sample types.

value.description: Measured value (a number or a descriptive string)

isHighlighted.description: True when the matched range colour is not GREEN

low.description: RANGE only. If only low, read as value < low.

high.description: RANGE only. If only high, read as value > high.

description.description: DESCRIPTIVE only. Value matches if it equals any entry.

ranges.description: All possible ranges for the test.

202.description: Values are not available yet and are being extracted from the report

example.message: Raw values for order 47585 are being extracted. Check back in a few minutes, or wait for the HARMONIZED_VALUES_CHANGED order webhook.

400.description: The call cannot return values. Returned when orderId is missing or invalid; when the order is CANCELED, so it will never reach REPORT_DELIVERED and retrying will not help; and when the order is in REPORT_DELIVERED but its values cannot be produced, in which case error says why.

example.error: Order 47585 is CANCELED and will never reach REPORT_DELIVERED, so it has no report values. Retrying will not change this.

409.description: The order exists and has not reached REPORT_DELIVERED yet but still can, so no values are available yet. The request is valid and can be repeated: retry later, or wait for the order STATUS_CHANGED webhook announcing REPORT_DELIVERED and call again then. A CANCELED order gets a 400 instead.

example.error: Order 47585 is not in REPORT_DELIVERED state yet

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Order id to get raw report values for. Only available when the order status is REPORT_DELIVERED.

get.description: Returns standardized test values for an order; available only when the order status is REPORT_DELIVERED. If the values have not been generated yet, the call first tries to retrieve them, which can take up to about 20 seconds, and returns them with a 200 when that succeeds. Otherwise, when the order has a valid report, extraction is started automatically and a 202 is returned — retry the call in a few minutes, or wait for the HARMONIZED_VALUES_CHANGED order webhook. Extraction is attempted at most once per order, so a 400 for an order in REPORT_DELIVERED means the values are not going to become available without LabStack support. A 409 means the order has not reached REPORT_DELIVERED yet but still can; retry later, or wait for the order STATUS_CHANGED webhook announcing REPORT_DELIVERED before calling. A CANCELED order never reaches REPORT_DELIVERED, so it gets a 400 and retrying will not help. testValues can include tests the report shows beyond those ordered.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Order id to get the report PDF of. Use 0 to download a dummy sample report.

get.description:
Returns the labs active for your store, each with its chain and the packages it offers from your store network.
type is the kind of center. A COLLECTION_CENTER is a sample-collection point that serves home sample collection and normally takes no center visits, so it does not do scans. A DIAGNOSTIC_CENTER or HOSPITAL takes center visits; which scans and other center tests it does depends on the tests it offers. Decide which services to offer at a lab from isHomeSampleSupported and isCenterVisitSupported rather than from type, and pass testIds or packageIds to checkServiceability or getSlots to find the labs that offer all of them.
